hypothesis: When both start_time and end_time are explicit, omit the Python default-duration metadata block; retain first_channel extraction and all downstream readers/rewinds.
interpretation: Nested cumulative profile times must not be added or treated as promised savings. GetTimeSeriesType includes two calls, one retained by _read_channel. Profile instrumentation and file-cache state can affect duration. MKL descriptor construction remains only a secondary observed target.

source_semantics.explicit_bounds: Existing cache time sieve and duration validation occur before metadata; actual _read_channel still performs channel type lookup and the LAL read.
source_semantics.default_bounds: Guard must be start_time is None or end_time is None, retaining the entire old block for any omitted bound, including explicit duration.
source_semantics.channels: Keep channels[0] extraction before the guard to preserve empty-list IndexError; preserve channel order, output list behavior and FrStreamSeek after each read.
source_semantics.cache_integrity: Preserve cache construction, regex/time sieve, verbose/checksum stream modes and FrStreamSetMode.
source_semantics.upstream_lal: Length and type wrappers query the current frame. Metadata fills the series without advancing the stream. The actual time-series reader seeks to the requested start and obtains metadata itself. These upstream files are not verified as the installed build; real-frame tests must confirm behavior.

required_evidence: Frozen minimal diff and relevant unit tests before timing
Real generated-frame values, dtype, epoch and delta_t, single/multiple channels, fractional/GPS and cross-frame explicit bounds
Default and duration cases, list/cache/sieve/integrity and existing validation behavior
Unchanged workload, actual strain and PSD hashes plus trigger gates
Contemporaneous baseline/candidate standard CPU and Torch CPU/CUDA process timings
